subject: C29
required_fixes: R1 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:196–223 and crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:133: verification does not implement C29's native workflow. A stored scan key becomes Pass without any service check; Gateway is always skipped; Red Team/Model selections are never checked. My scan-only probe dispatched zero verification operations yet announced 'All checks passed.' Implement native-owned verification over the admitted checks for the selected products, with truthful unavailable/unverified results and product-specific warnings. Acceptance: invalid or untested credentials cannot produce a verified Pass; selected products receive actual results or explicit incomplete coverage, and warnings retain the correct product.

R2 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:127–163,234–254 and docs/architecture/ui-v2/provenance.md:P27: creating/selecting the tenant and importing cases before completion violates the required cancel transaction. The native N05 evidence confirms Cancel keeps a second tenant active; its assertion has been changed to expect that violation. Provide a native draft/completion boundary implementing completeOnboarding/addTenant semantics. Acceptance: Cancel at every add step leaves tenants, active selection, products and cases unchanged, except an already-vaulted credential exposed as removable/unattached; successful completion commits the intended setup and switches once.

R3 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:320–400,463: 'Fix and verify again' cannot repair a saved but invalid client or mistaken tenant details. Once a tenant exists the profile form disappears, and ready credentials hide their entry controls. My failure-board probe returned to Tenant with no profile form, Client ID or Client secret input. Acceptance: a failed authentication or wrong TSG/region can be corrected or the optional client removed within onboarding, followed by a fresh successful verification without abandoning setup.

R4 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:89–109,196–225,272–279,419: there is no validation signature or downstream invalidation. After a successful Runtime-only check, selecting Gateway leaves 'All checks passed' and Continue enabled; visited Done remains directly reachable after edits. Verification also lacks a generation guard for overlapping runs. Acceptance: changes to products, tenant details, credentials or context invalidate results and downstream completion eligibility; stale asynchronous results cannot restore it, and current inputs must be verified before completion.

R5 — apps/desktop/src/app.tsx:172–185 and apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:336: first-run v1 import is unreachable. The button dispatches navigate(import), but App continues rendering Wizard whenever onboarding is incomplete. A production-App probe pushed activeFeature=import and still displayed 'Your tenant.' Acceptance: a fresh user can enter the reviewed C23 import flow from this action and return to credential setup without bypassing import review or importing authentication.

R6 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:476–481: the Academy step cannot complete the hosted device flow. Awaiting approval shows a code without the verification URL or openAcademyVerification action; failed/starting/completing states are presented as 'Signed out', and a failed flow has no retry. The native sign-in task does not open the browser automatically. Acceptance: exercise start, open approved verification page, pending, completion, failure/retry and cancel/skip through the existing Academy contract, with accurate status and no local account authority.

R7 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:106–109,243–254: onboarding transition outcomes are ignored. When finishTenantSetup is admitted but setOnboarding(done) is refused, my probe called onClose, displayed no error and left the disabled 'Opening…' control indefinitely. The welcome transition is also fire-and-forget. Acceptance: refusal, failed delivery and unknown delivery at either transition remain visible and recoverable; completion closes only after native confirmation, without duplicating warning/import effects.

R8 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:111–114,400: Back on add mode's initial Tenant step calls go(-1). My production-component probe then had no heading and no current step. Bound transitions and omit Back where no preceding step exists. Acceptance: every enabled navigation action produces a valid step with a meaningful focus target in both modes.

R9 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:414–438 and crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:3365–3374: all products can be unchecked and the UI permits completing every remaining step, then sends products:[], which Rust refuses. Selecting only Gateway also produces a summary that omits Runtime although Rust forcibly adds it. Acceptance: presentation and native selection rules agree, an invalid empty choice is prevented/explained at Products, and the summary exactly matches the committed selection.

R10 — apps/desktop/src/v2/v2-shell.tsx:242, apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:260–261 and apps/desktop/src/v2/modal.tsx:103–127: the add sheet exceeds the visible viewport without a bounded scrolling layout. The retained 1280×820 AX window ends at screen y=857, while Cancel starts at y=892; the screenshot clips its footer. Acceptance: the entire workflow, including visible Cancel and primary actions, remains reachable at the supported minimum and 100%/200% zoom in both themes, with keyboard focus scrolled into view.

R11 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:320–438,468–473: substantial reviewed screen content is absent: environment selection/context, optional Gateway workspace setup, tenant-derived licence state, and per-selected-product starter packs/counts. Add mode also requires a scan key despite P17 retaining optional credentials there. P28 records a deferral rather than implementing these requirements. Acceptance: provide the specified inputs and observed states, permit the reviewed add-mode credential choices, and import only explicitly selected packs with their counts; any scope reduction requires an accepted contract change rather than a passing fixture for omitted behavior.

R12 — crates/desktop-core/src/features.rs:65, packages/desktop-contracts/src/generated/SetupWarning.ts and packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:340: recordedSecs is generated as bigint, but JSON and the validator return a number. My DesktopClient probe accepted a numeric timestamp; a consumer using the declared bigint arithmetic threw a TypeError. Acceptance: Rust serialization, generated declarations and runtime validation agree on one safe representation, with a populated-warning round-trip test through DesktopClient.
